contexts.text: Rational truth separated from rational good. Described.
Rational good never fights, however attacked, because it is mild, gentle, patient, and yielding... yet it conquers everybody. It never even thinks about fighting, nor glories in victory...
The Lord's rational good conjoined with His truth. Signified, Explained.
The conjunction of natural good with rational good. Signified, Explained.
Rational good must be made conformable with natural good so as to make a one; (otherwise) Divine perception is impossible.
That rational good... also would put off the human. Signified, Explained.
Human rational good has in it much from worldly delights...
Under Rational, see this reference. AC 3030. AC 3209:2. AC 3573. AC 3579. AC 3677. AC 4038:3.
Enriched with rational goods and natural goods. Signified.
The veil = the proximate and inmost appearances of rational good and truth, in which are the Angels of the Third Heaven.

The Divine good in the Rational (Isaac) was born (from the Divine truth itself conjoined with the Divine good); and was not good separated from truth, but was Divine good with Divine truth; and both together are called good in the Rational to which was to be conjoined truth from the natural man (Rebekah). AC 3194. AC 3195.
In these two verses is described the state of rational good, when it is in expectation of truth, with which it is to be conjoined. These states exist continually...
That rational good brought with it the truth into the sanctuary of truth. Signified, Explained.
Between rational good, and the truth called forth from the Natural... there is not a marriage, but a covenant. Signified, Explained.
The Natural as to good is conceived from the good of the Rational as a father; and as to truth, is conceived from the truth of the Rational as a mother.

That the Divine good of the Rational loved the good which pertained to the Natural, and that the Divine truth of the Divine Rational loved the truth which pertained to the Natural. Signified, Explained. (Continued. See Influx.) Hence there is a closer conjunction of the good of the Rational with the good of the Natural, than with its truth; and of the truth of the Rational with the truth of the Natural, than with its good. Signified.
Therefore, where there are no truths... there is no rational or human good, consequently, no spiritual life.
Increase as to rational good, and as to natural good. Signified, Explained.
With those not hypocrites, rational good appears in the face from a certain fire of life; and rational truth from the light of this lire.
For in this state rational truth is not so well conjoined with rational good...
The good of the Natural comes forth solely from... the good of the Rational... and therefore the truth of the Natural also is thence. (Continued. See Influx.)
That the good of the Rational conjoins with itself good first, and truth afterwards, and this through the Natural. Signified, Explained.
Ends of good... are what is called the Rational as to good, or the good of the Rational. (Thus) such as is the Rational as to good, such is the Natural which invests it.

When the state is such, the Rational as to good conjoins itself immediately with the good of the Natural; and, through this, with its truths; and also mediately, through truth conjoined with itself in the Rational, with the truth of the Natural; and, through this, with the good there. Thus the conjunction becomes indissoluble.
For (the truth of good) could not be produced by immediate influx from the good of the Rational, unless at the same time by mediate, that is, through the truth of the Rational...
That the good of the Rational conjoined itself inmostly with the good of the Natural; and, through the good there, with the truth. Signified, Explained.

(After the conjunction) the good of the Rational inflows immediately into the good of the Natural; and, through the good, into the truth of it; and also mediately, through the truth of the Rational into the truth of the Natural; and, through this, into the good there. Signified.
See Natural good.
Some of these Knowledges inflow immediately through the good of the Rational...
All the goods and truths in the natural man are conceived and born... of the good of the Rational as a father, and of the truth of the Rational as a mother.
Good rational and natural destroyed. Signified.
No grapes in the vine = no interior or rational good.
Grapes in the desert = rational good not yet made spiritual.
Rational truths and goods profaned. Signified, Explained.
